a.text: The reactor of a United Starline starship still burns so brightly.
Since the atmosphere control center crashed, we've been shrouded in dull gray clouds. A radiant sight like this certainly lifts the spirit.

To my pleasant surprise, Valeria was also on the starship. I discovered once she landed that she had come to bid farewell to her mother. Ever since joining the stargate modification project, she has been completely absorbed in her duties. It was surprising to see her still concerned with worldly matters.
If she still has a mind for such things, perhaps we might finally talk about that wedding that's been put on hold for the past ten years?
…I soon dismissed that thought as foolish. The woman I once knew now stood before me like a stranger. I could no longer discern what she was thinking.
As she stood before her mother's life support pod, her expression was one I had never seen before. It was neither sorrow nor regret... it was envy.
What could she possibly envy about her dying mother? Was it the peaceful release offered by the machine's simulated world?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: You're still here, Jordi? Everyone else has left...

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Sorry, I didn't know there would be a tribunal today.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: That's okay.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The search logs... you've asked quite a few questions. 'How big is the ocean?' 'Is it bigger than the land?' 'By how much?'

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: 'Can Ægir cities float to the surface?'

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: 'How do the Ægir tell whether it's day or night?'

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Is this how you've been trying to understand Ægir? I fear it may confuse you even more.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Mr. Avitus... I'm not sure why, but I feel really excited.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: In the Inquisition's nautical charts, the ocean extends only a few nautical miles from shore before giving way to unknown regions marked in grayish-blue.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: In some areas, we couldn't even get near the shore.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But your charts are so detailed. Geological features, energy pockets, local fauna and flora... There are so many pages, I don't even know where to start.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The forests at the heart of the ocean, icebergs that never melt, thermal vents deep in the trenches...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: For a moment, I thought that the land, sea, and sky were all mine for the taking, that I need simply reach out. Like everything was made for me.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Sorry, that sounds really arrogant, doesn't it?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Quite the opposite, young man. It is but a most basic desire.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But I...
The young Ægir looks up and gazes at the coral-shaped terminal. Holographic images and words leap up and down, illuminating his soft eyes.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I've been in Milliarium for a whole day now.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But I can't handle your tech, I don't get your discussions, and I'm even lost with directions.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The tribunal that just happened... I have no idea how you guys settled your disagreement.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I did a search for Breogan, the ship designer, who I thought was my ancestor. I saw his face, heard his voice, and looked at his designs.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Is there really anything I have in common with him? Would his descendants really turn out to be someone... like me?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I couldn't find a single sign that says I belong here.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ægir is like a lighthouse, bright and tall. I always knew it existed, but when I finally followed its light and reached its base...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Why do I feel lost instead?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Breogan. It's been many years since his name was last spoken.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: He was a remarkable man, even amongst the Ægir. He was the most talented designer in the Academy of Technology, but left everything behind to go ashore, right when his country needed him most.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Even this city is connected to him, albeit in a somewhat unusual way.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: How so?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: It was through this city that he went on land. The Institute of Development Planning even tried to penalize a few consuls for failing to stop him.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Listen, Jordi. I cannot ascertain whether you are truly bound to him by blood, though such a connection holds little significance.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: What matters is that there can be no doubt that you are Ægir.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I know I am. But how do I prove I belong here, if I can't even trace my own heritage?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: A true Ægir needs no proof of that.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: But I understand. We all search for answers in the past.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: I'm no different.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: I can say with a straight face that I am one of Ægir's foremost authorities on prehistory. I firmly believe in the weight of history, and that it contains truths and patterns that will show us the way forward.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: (Mutters) But what if its a way of destined destruction for Ægir?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...I'm sorry, what was that last part?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Huh? Did you say something, Doctor?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Sorry. I was just thinking about Shark and Swordfish.

options: They're probably on a killing spree right now.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm not worried about them. They're strong.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Nothing good ever happened to those around me, which is why I was always alone—until I joined Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Now it's happening again.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Thank you.

options: Are you afraid you'll bring disaster to the Hunters?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Maybe.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: But we hunters aren't afraid of the bad end we might bring to each other.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Because we all share the same grim fate, we can trust each other with our lives.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: This time though, it might not be just the Hunters.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I could bring disaster to all of Ægir.

options: You won't. I believe in you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: That's what Captain Ulpianus always said.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: He would explain our battle plans in great detail to everyone else, but with me, he simply said he believed in me.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...He believed I could complete my mission even if I couldn't memorize those complex strategies.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: He was always so reliable and had an answer for everything.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I remember the songs he wrote before battles. He said we could use them as codes to communicate because the Seaborn didn't understand music.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: But I just liked the songs.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: He had a great sense of direction, too. He could always lead us all back, even when we were lost in those maze-like nests.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: We could always count on him to point the way, until...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes. The 1st and 4th Companies sacrificed themselves to clear a path, while the 2nd held off the Seaborn that were rushing back.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Captain Ulpianus led the charge and soon arrived at the target, the core organ of the Firstborn.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Then we lost his signal.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I thought he was dead, so it fell to me to deal the killing blow.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yeah. I don't know what happened that day.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I still don't know why he didn't come back.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: And the more I don't know, the more I feel like I need to do something.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Ha. Rush in with a 'woosh', knock them down with a 'pow', and finish them with a 'thud'.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I remember.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Arrived at target coordinates.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: We came as fast as we could. Though not fast enough, it seems.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: This is a graveyard.
Giant shipwrecks and Seaborn remains lie entangled in a grotesque embrace. Pale flakes descend like snow.
While some have given it a more romanticized name, marine snow, it does little to hide its cruel nature: fragments of organic matter, both Seaborn and human.
The sweetness of blood and the stench of death, intensified by the cannon's lingering heat, spread with the falling flakes.
The Abyssal Hunters' strong sense of smell magnifies all of this, and Specter cannot help but cover her nose.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: This shouldn't be unfamiliar to you, Shark.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The fleet pins down the Seaborn with superior numbers as the Hunters flank and eliminate the swarm's core. We've used this tactic often.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: This is the same scene we see each time we leave their nest.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I know... perhaps we've spent too much time on land.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: It's not a pleasant thing to recall.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: One engineering mothership, ten battleships, numerous smaller ships... The wreckage positions on the seabed indicate they stayed in formation. They were not taken by surprise.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: There are signs of gravitational distortion on nearby rocks. They tried to stop the Seaborn using force fields.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But the Seaborn were faster. The ships weren't even able to form a crossfire.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: They fought with them in close quarters...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Something's not right.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The squadron's destination was Nest 37, but all the ships appear to be headed for Milliarium.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Besides, now that the squadron is destroyed, why haven't the Seaborn made their next move?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Swordfish.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Ngh—

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Ugh—

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Alright, grab my hand.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I did tell you to stay on the corvette.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Deep-water equipment may keep you from being crushed by the water pressure, but even the Ægir are at the mercy of the ocean currents without proper training.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I could use some help, once you're done laughing.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Imagine you're dancing with a rowdy partner. Counter her moves and find your balance. This is how you fight the currents.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: You're light. It shouldn't be hard for you.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: ...Don't look at me like that.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I'll meet you up ahead.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: A broken lighting array...

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Trace amounts of organic tissue on the broken metal frame... Human, and Seaborn.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Find anything?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Some tissue that matches the sample provided by the Institute of Development Planning. It's Tullia.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Milliarium was parked here around 40 hours ago. Based on the location of the array, she had left from the circulation system's sewage exit at the edge of the city.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: ...But why did she leave?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: It's hard to reconstruct the scene with what's available. The currents have already washed away most of the clues.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I'm afraid we won't find out if Tullia was a cultist with a grudge against the Waterway Program or what happened to her from here.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: This is two hours away by ship from Milliarium's present location. Even with deep-water equipment...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: She couldn't have swum back.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Based on the remaining tissues, it seems she had encountered a Seaborn.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: There's no way she could have survived.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: A dead end.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: That's... the direction the Abyssal Hunters went.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The battle may be fiercer than expected.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The Waterway Program is in its final phase. Once Nest 37 has been located, we can clear the Seaborn from this entire area and open up a Waterway.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: This can't just be a coincidence...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Could the incident with Tullia have something to do with the attack on the fleet?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Or maybe her incident is just a red fin to distract the Sea Patrol.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: There are too many new uncertainties, as if everything's sucked in a giant vortex.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: ...Let's go back to the city for now.

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Hard bank to port, full speed ahead! Go around that ridge and turn back. That should lose a third of the Seaborn on our tail.

steps.name: Ægir Soldier
steps.text: Ngh—

steps.name: Ægir Soldier
steps.text: Sir, the Seaborn have breached the hull!

steps.name: Ægir Soldier
steps.text: They're inside the ship!

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Keep the evasive maneuvers going, helmsman! We'll deal with the ones inside.

steps.name: Ægir Soldier
steps.text: Camouflage coating down to 10%! We'll be fully visible soon!

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Buy as much time as you can!

steps.name: Ægir Soldier
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Gugh—

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Take care of the rest, Shark.

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Abyssal Hunters?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Gladiia.

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: I recognize you, ma'am.

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Have the other ships made it safely back to Milliarium, Madame Consul?

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Thank goodness...

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: The more of our elites we save, the more strength we'll have for what's ahead.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Are you the commander of this vessel?

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: We were ambushed. A large swarm of Seaborn left their nests and appeared on the squadron's route... Virtually unheard of in previous beacon deployments.

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: We couldn't reveal our battle plans. We had to retreat.

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Our ship was the fastest in the fleet. The most logical tactic was for us to delay the Seaborn while the main fleet retreated.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How many survivors are there on your ship?

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Twenty-six... Less than one in ten.

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Why the silence, Madame Consul?

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I'm sorry, commander. Your ship and your twenty-six men are the only survivors.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: All Seaborn inside the ship have been eliminated.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: There's no better way to tell you, so I'll make it brief... the thousand or so men whose retreat you were covering fell into an even bigger ambush.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: We happened to see your ship weaving through the complex terrain as we arrived.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But what you couldn't have seen is the Seaborn had you completely surrounded. You were just chasing your own tail in their trap.

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: We failed the mission.

steps.name: Ægir Officer
steps.text: Yet we were the ones who lived. The losses are... much worse than expected...

spans.text: were the ones who lived. The losses are... much worse than expected...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But you did live.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Lift your head, Ægir.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You and your men are just as much Ægir's elites, and you will give your strength to what's ahead.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: For now, Laurentina and I will bring you back to the city.
